purpose_and_use.text: Monthly behavioural probability of default (PD) for existing credit card accounts, used for limit management and collections prioritisation (per the header comment). Scores are exported to a CSV for the limit-management engine. The code does not state how collections prioritisation consumes the score, nor any cut-offs or strategies. The PD is a 12-month bad probability only if the 'bad' definition and outcome window are applied as intended (see limitations).

evidence.quote: Purpose : Monthly behavioural PD for existing credit card accounts, used for
/* 4. Export scores for the limit-management engine */

data.text: Three warehouse tables from library CRDW (/data/warehouse/cards) are merged by account_id: crdw.account_month (filtered to month_id = &perf_month., i.e. 202312, with 'if a' keeping only accounts present in that table), crdw.bureau_monthly (bureau_score, num_searches_6m) and crdw.delinquency_flags (worst_status_12m). Observation month is hard-coded as 202312. Target: bad_flag = 1 if worst_status_12m >= 3, else 0. The macro variable outcome_window = 12 is declared but not referenced anywhere in the code. There is NO train/test/validation split: the model is fitted and scored on the same dataset (work.base_binned). No sample size, bad rate or exclusion rules (e.g. closed or dormant accounts) are coded. The header notes the library and tables are synthetic and do not exist, so the program was never run.

evidence.quote: if worst_status_12m >= 3 then bad_flag = 1; else bad_flag = 0;

methodology.text: Binary logistic regression (PROC LOGISTIC, descending so that bad_flag=1 is the modelled event) with stepwise variable selection at slentry=0.05 and slstay=0.05. Candidate predictors: util_band and mob_band (categorical, reference-cell parameterisation), payment_ratio, bureau_score and num_searches_6m (continuous, entered as-is). Utilisation and months on book are coarse-classed into 4 and 3 bands respectively via PROC FORMAT. The code does not derive points, a score scale (e.g. points-to-double-odds) or any PD calibration step; the output p_1 is the raw predicted probability from the fitted model, which is exported as the score. Which variables survive selection is determined at run time and is not recorded in the material.

implementation.text: Single SAS program using DATA steps, PROC FORMAT, PROC LOGISTIC and PROC EXPORT. Steps in order: (1) build base table by merging three CRDW tables and deriving features and target; (2) define formats and create binned variables; (3) fit stepwise logistic regression, saving the fitted model to model.bhv_cc_01_fit and scoring the same data to model.bhv_cc_01_scored; (4) export account_id and p_1 to /exports/bhv_cc_01_scores.csv. Inputs: crdw.account_month, crdw.bureau_monthly, crdw.delinquency_flags. Outputs: model.bhv_cc_01_fit, model.bhv_cc_01_scored, /exports/bhv_cc_01_scores.csv. No random seed is used (no stochastic step). Run by executing the program in a SAS session with the CRDW and MODEL libnames resolvable. The code has no scheduling or orchestration, so how the 'monthly' run is triggered is not shown. It was not executed in this review (no SAS runtime; tables are synthetic).

Performance cannot be stated. Because scoring is done on the development data with no holdout, any in-sample performance obtained from this code would be optimistic.

variables.name: account_id
variables.description: Account key used for merging the three source tables and exported with the score.
variables.transformation: Used as BY variable in merge; kept in export.

variables.name: month_id
variables.description: Observation month on account_month; filtered to &perf_month. (202312). Also kept from bureau_monthly.

variables.name: balance
variables.description: Account balance; numerator of utilisation. Raw variable not itself a model candidate.

variables.name: credit_limit
variables.description: Credit limit; denominator of utilisation (floored at 1).

variables.name: utilisation
variables.description: Balance to limit ratio, capped at 1.5; source for util_band.

variables.name: util_band
variables.description: Categorical utilisation band: <30%, 30-70%, 70-90%, 90%+. Candidate predictor (class variable, reference parameterisation).

variables.name: payment_amt
variables.description: Payment amount made; numerator of payment_ratio.

variables.name: min_payment_due
variables.description: Minimum payment due; denominator of payment_ratio (floored at 1).

variables.name: payment_ratio
variables.description: Payment to minimum-due ratio, capped at 10. Continuous candidate predictor.
variables.evidence: model bad_flag = util_band mob_band payment_ratio bureau_score num_searches_6m

variables.name: open_date
variables.description: Account opening date; used to derive months_on_book.
variables.transformation: intck('month', open_date, perf month as date)

variables.name: months_on_book
variables.description: Months between account opening and observation month; source for mob_band.
variables.transformation: intck month count, then binned via mob_fmt.

variables.name: mob_band
variables.description: Categorical months-on-book band: <1y, 1-3y, 3y+. Candidate predictor (class variable).

variables.name: bureau_score
variables.description: Bureau score from bureau_monthly. Continuous candidate predictor, entered untransformed.

variables.name: num_searches_6m
variables.description: Number of bureau searches in the last 6 months (name-implied). Continuous candidate predictor, untransformed.

variables.name: worst_status_12m
variables.description: Worst delinquency status over the 12 months from delinquency_flags; used only to derive the target, not a predictor.
variables.evidence: if worst_status_12m >= 3 then bad_flag = 1; else bad_flag = 0;

variables.name: bad_flag
variables.description: Default indicator: 1 if worst_status_12m >= 3, else 0. Modelled event is bad_flag=1 (descending option).

variables.name: p_1
variables.description: Predicted probability of bad_flag=1 produced by the SCORE statement (output field, not an input); exported as the score.

transformations.description: Merge crdw.account_month (filtered to month_id = 202312, 'if a' keeps only accounts present there), crdw.bureau_monthly (account_id, month_id, bureau_score, num_searches_6m) and crdw.delinquency_flags (account_id, worst_status_12m) by account_id.
Month count between open_date and the performance month (202312 converted to a date via yymmn6.).

transformations.evidence: if worst_status_12m >= 3 then bad_flag = 1; else bad_flag = 0;

transformations.step: Coarse classing of months on book

transformations.description: PROC LOGISTIC (descending) with stepwise selection at 0.05 entry and 0.05 stay; scores the same dataset to produce p_1.
Write account_id and p_1 to CSV for the limit-management engine.

assumptions.text: A worst delinquency status of 3 or more in the 12 months is an appropriate 'bad' definition for behavioural PD. The status scale (what 3 represents, e.g. 90+ days past due) is not defined in the material.
assumptions.evidence: if worst_status_12m >= 3 then bad_flag = 1; else bad_flag = 0;

assumptions.text: Delinquency over the 12 months covered by worst_status_12m is treated as the outcome for accounts observed at 202312. Whether that window lies after the observation month (a true outcome) or before it (a lookback) is not established by the code.
Caps (utilisation at 1.5, payment ratio at 10) and floors (denominators at 1) are assumed adequate treatment of outliers and zero denominators; no justification is documented.
Linear-in-logit effects are assumed for payment_ratio, bureau_score and num_searches_6m, which enter unbinned.
assumptions.evidence: model bad_flag = util_band mob_band payment_ratio bureau_score num_searches_6m

limitations.text: No holdout, out-of-time or cross-validation sample: the model is fitted and scored on the same data, so overfitting and in-sample bias cannot be assessed from this code, and stepwise selection exacerbates this risk.

Single observation month (202312) hard-coded, so the development sample reflects one point in the cycle only; no through-the-cycle or seasonality treatment and no mechanism to roll the month forward is coded.

outcome_window macro is declared but unused, so the stated 12-month outcome horizon is not enforced by the code; the bad definition relies entirely on the pre-built worst_status_12m field whose timing relative to the observation month is unclear.

Possible look-ahead / leakage risk: worst_status_12m is merged by account_id only (no month_id alignment) with delinquency_flags and bureau_monthly, so merge timing alignment is not controlled; bureau_monthly month_id is kept but not used in the BY statement.

The output p_1 is the raw model probability with no calibration to a central tendency, no scorecard scaling, and no PD floor or cap or segmentation; it is described as a PD but regulatory or IFRS 9 suitability is not demonstrated.

Missing-value handling is not coded: PROC LOGISTIC drops observations with missing predictors by default, and the base merge can produce missing bureau or delinquency fields for unmatched accounts, so excluded or unscored accounts may occur silently.
No documentation beyond code comments, no validation and no monitoring evidence exist; the program cannot be reproduced here as the data and SAS runtime are unavailable.
